layers.label: Black-hole shadow
layers.explanation: The dark region against the bright gas — not the hole itself, but the boundary from which no light returns: the silhouette of the event horizon.

layers.label: Accretion disk
layers.explanation: Gas spiraling in, heated by compression until it glows — orange on the inside, fading to pale blue-white far out.

hotspots.label: Singularity — the collapsed core
hotspots.description: Where the collapsing core's matter has been crushed to a point of essentially infinite density — hidden forever behind the horizon.

hotspots.label: Event horizon — the no-return boundary
hotspots.description: The sphere where escape needs light speed: inside, nothing can ever come out. It looks like a shadow in the light of the disk.

hotspots.label: Accretion disk — the doomed whirl
hotspots.description: Gas spiraling inward and heating as it falls — the glow you actually see, wrapping the shadow like a horizontal whirlpool.

hotspots.label: Photon ring — bent light
hotspots.description: Light from behind the hole bent around it into a thin, bright ring — the famous 'ring of fire' in the first black-hole photo.

hotspots.label: Tidal stretch (spaghettification)
hotspots.description: A small probe stretched into a thread as it falls — near-side gravity pulling harder than far-side, drawn as a thin smear of light.

visualStyleNotes: Clean scientific-illustration look (Anatomy Atelier): black shadow disk centered, bright tilted accretion ring in warm orange fading to pale blue, photon ring as a hair-thin bright circle, faint lensed star field behind arcs slightly. Nothing grotesque; the spaghettification is a stylized thin light streak, not gore.
materialNotes: Disk: additive glow material with radial falloff, tilt ~15°. Shadow: pure black sphere with no light response. Photon ring: thin emissive ring. Background: subtle star points that curve near the hole to show lensing.
assetBrief: Procedural Three.js scene: black sphere (shadow), tilted glowing disk, thin photon ring, background star field with subtle lensing arcs. Auto-rotate on; hotspots at listed positions. All other conventions match the stars set.
